payload.summary: Formulation strength badges take the last number in a listed range, so a multi-strength product badges one arbitrary strength
payload.detail: DEPENDS ON PR #2580, WHICH HAD NOT MERGED WHEN THIS WAS WRITTEN, and the dependency is stated first because everything below assumes it. Verified on origin/main at cc5ebcf on 2026-09-03: src/lib/medication-badges.ts:104 still reads /(\d+)\s*mg/i, so on main the HIGHER-RISK H1 defect is live — varenicline "Tablets (0.5 mg, 1 mg)" badges as "5 mg", a tenfold misread. H1 is an audit finding in docs/audit/full-repository-audit-2026-09-02.md and is NOT a row in this ledger, so nothing here closes it and nothing here should be read as closing it. IF PR #2580 IS CLOSED WITHOUT MERGING, raise H1 as its own P1 row before acting on this one: this row is the lesser defect and must never be worked ahead of it. THIS ROW, assuming #2580 lands: H1 fixes the decimal and concentration cases and leaves the list-tail shape untouched, which #2580's own reviewer flagged as pre-existing rather than introduced. Morphine's "Tablets IR (10, 20 mg)" badges as "20 mg tablet". The number is a real strength of a real product, so this is not H1's tenfold misread, but the choice of which strength to show is arbitrary and a clinician glancing at the badge is given no signal that 10 mg also exists. Scope not yet measured: only the morphine case is confirmed, and the first step is to count how many of the 328 catalogue records state a comma-separated or hyphenated strength list in their formulation text. FIX candidates, in preference order: (a) render the full range when a formulation states more than one strength, so the badge reads the same as the source, (b) suppress the badge for multi-strength products, matching the conservative choice H1 already made for concentration-only and combination products. Do NOT simply switch the regex from the last match to the first without deciding the question, since that is equally arbitrary in the other direction. GUARD, corrected: main's tests/medication-badges.test.ts has no formulation-strength invariant — its "keeps badge lists stable across the full snapshot corpus" case checks badge-list stability, not strength parsing. The corpus-wide assertion that a badged number must be a whole strength token and not a concentration arrives WITH #2580. Confirm it is present before relying on it, and if #2580 did not land, write the focused regression assertion as part of this work rather than assuming a guard exists.
payload.source: Reviewer note on PR #2580 (audit fixes P1, finding H1), recorded 2026-09-03; the same PR body carries it as a suggested follow-up finding. The #2580 dependency and the corrected guard statement come from Codex's P2 review of PR #2585 (the PR queueing this request), verified against origin/main cc5ebcf before amending.
